column3: NASB supplies “to me” and “not” in the oath (“if I do not make your life”).
The Hebrew “he saw” is rendered “he was afraid,” following another vocalization; “went for his life” is rendered “ran for his life.”
“Broom plant” is rendered “juniper tree,” and “asked his soul to die” as “requested for himself that he might die.”
“Of hot coals” is rendered “baked on hot stones,” and “jug” as “jar.” NASB adds “again.”
“The cave” is rendered “a cave,” and “What is to you here?” as “What are you doing here?”
“I have certainly been zealous” is rendered “I have been very zealous.”
“A sound of a soft whisper” is rendered “a sound of a gentle blowing.”
“What is to you here?” is rendered “What are you doing here?”
NASB supplies “of oxen,” and “two and the ten” as “the twelfth.”
“Go, turn back” is rendered “Go back again.”
